hook_text: Four tests decide whether a shelter fabric is safe. Three use water. The fourth, only the teacher does.
clip_script: Plain canvas: drip water on it and it is through in a minute. Two fixes. Repel: wax, oil or silicone on every fibre, so drops bead and roll off; it breathes, it is cheap, but press a wet knee on it and it leaks. Coat: acrylic or PVC as a solid film; nothing gets through, nothing breathes, so you need vents. Sew a seam and it leaks at every hole until you tape it. Now the candle, teacher only, tongs, sand, water. Cotton catches and burns to ash. Waxed cotton burns hotter. Polyester melts into a dripping bead. Tarpaulin drips burning drops. PVC chars and stops, then smokes poison. Wool chars and goes out. Treated canvas chars and goes out. Put it all in a table, safety first: a flame-retardant coated canvas on top, cheap tarpaulin on the floor, every seam sealed. Tested, not guessed.
visual_style: Whiteboard funnel dripping onto a clamped square; beads rolling off; a thumb pressing a wet square on a towel; a seam with droplets at each stitch; candle results in a row; a choice table.
mood: Experimental and careful, a lab bench with a purpose.
pacing: Drip, repel, coat, seam, candle results, table, each a beat.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and run the drip and pressure tests on a fabric at home.
